Text.Text: The conduits are singing steady, and so are you. The current runs through you now -- both blades, one river, pooling nowhere. Come sit in the ward sometimes when your hands are empty. Healing is the same flow, pointed gently.
You're trying to carry all the motion yourself. Reach rank 50 in Saberstaff, then come back. We need a steadier foundation before I ask you to let the Force through it.

The Force moves through a place like water. Six Infinite Conduit adepts have trapped it in the Medical Sublevel and called the pressure strength. Defeat those six and bring me their triage ledger. I want to know how long they've been doing this around the patients.
Take the key to the entrance in the Abandoned Warehouse. It leads into the Medical Sublevel. Keep your grip light; you may need to change direction sooner than you expect.

Most saber forms gather the Force and spend it in bursts. The conduit never gathers. The current passes through you -- into one blade, out the other, endlessly. Nothing pooled, nothing hoarded, nothing lost. It is the gentlest form I know and the least forgiving to learn, because the moment you try to keep any of it, it stops being a current and starts being a wound.
The entrance to the Medical Sublevel is in the Abandoned Warehouse on Dantooine. Take my key there. Keep your company close when you enter so no one gets left upstairs.

Adepts who learned to hold the current instead of carrying it. Their strikes land heavier than they should, and they do not yield -- a dammed current doesn't know how to stop, only how to break. Don't try to outlast them; end each one cleanly and move on. And mind the kolto lines. The ward above still breathes through them.
The six adepts are in Dantooine's Medical Sublevel. Bring their ledger here to the Medical Interior. There is no need to hurry past a patient.
You're back -- and the current under the floor sounds looser already. That's the ledger under your arm, water-stained and all. May I?

Thank you. No -- don't wave that off. A ward runs on its ledger the way a form runs on breath. Six of theirs are quiet below, and forty of mine are safer above. Take the credits, drink some water, and rest. The current has more to show you.

Five specialists use the sublevel's kolto coupler to sustain their practice. They've tied care to a lesson that won't let anything rest. Beat the five and bring me the coupler. We can let the ward breathe again.
Return to the sublevel. Leave yourself room to change the turn; their practice depends on you staying in it.

On the line, it lets two currents join without turbulence -- kolto or the Force, the principle is the same. In their hands it's a choke: starve the flow, then open it all at once and call the surge strength. Surge is not strength. It is debt, collected violently. Bring it back and the line will forgive everything.
The entrance to the Medical Sublevel is in the Abandoned Warehouse on Dantooine. Take my key there. Keep your company close when you enter so no one gets left upstairs.

Specialists, not students. They ride the surge -- long stillness, then everything at once. Between surges they are slow, almost gentle. That is your moment, and they know it, so they will try to make you impatient. Be water. Wait with them. Then don't.
Five specialists in the sublevel have the kolto coupler. Beat them and bring it back to me.
I felt the pressure even out before dawn -- the whole ward exhaled at once. You have it, then. Let me see.

Not even scorched. The line takes it back tonight, and the ward sleeps to a steady hum for the first time in weeks. You're learning the form the right way round -- flow first, blades after. Rest now. The next current runs colder.

The warden won't yield the Medical Sublevel. Challenge him there, defeat him, and bring back his ward sigil. Ask companions to join you if you can. Someone beside you can notice the pressure you're too busy bearing.

Good. When you face him, remember -- he must hold everything, and you must hold nothing. Let his weight be his problem. Strike, release, let a companion strike while you breathe. The sigil never leaves him; it will come up with you or not at all.

A ward-keeper, once. One of ours. When the others began damming the current, he chose not to join them -- he chose to exceed them, to hold every drop of the deep ward's flow inside himself. What is left is a reservoir shaped like a man. There is a person in there somewhere. The pressure speaks for him now.
He answers the challenge marker in the Medical Sublevel. Rest before you call him. I'd rather you arrived with strength to spare than with a story about how quickly you got there.

He hits hard and recovers well. Watch the pause after he commits; it may be the only quiet part of the exchange. If you've brought company, let them take his attention while you recover, and do the same for them.
Call the warden at the Medical Sublevel's challenge marker. Defeat him and recover the ward sigil.
The held breath is gone. The whole sublevel let it out in the night, and I have been smiling at pipes all morning like a fool. Sit down first -- sit. Now. The sigil.

Fractured, and it held its shape anyway. Most of us do. I will consecrate the deep ward again this week, and his name goes back on the keepers' wall -- the old name, from before. That mercy was yours, and you did it wisely: with others. Keep those people close. The last doors down there do not open for one pair of hands.
Four keepers still have the matron's token. They're using her authority to keep the conduits closed. Defeat the four in the sublevel and recover it. The ward ought to belong to its patients again.
Recover the matron's token. The ward has waited long enough for someone to put it back to work.

The first four I ever taught the conduit form. That is the wound underneath all of this, and now you know it. They understood the current perfectly and trusted it not at all -- and mistrust, in the end, is just a dam you build out of yourself. They are better than anything you have faced below, except perhaps the warden. Together, they may be better than him.
The four keepers are in the Medical Sublevel. They have the matron's token. Bring it back to me when they're defeated; the ward can use her authority for care again.

Four currents braided into one defense. Press one and another answers. Unbraid them if you can; if you cannot, bring companions and braid your own. And spare the station itself -- every line in the sublevel crosses that room, and the ward above drinks from those pipes while you fight.
Four keepers in the sublevel still have the matron's token. Bring it here after they're defeated.
I know that weight from across a room. She wore it thirty years, and it never once sat well in proud hands. Yours aren't. Give it here -- gently.

Then only the deepest room is left. The matron who wore this saved more lives than I can count without ever raising a blade, and she taught me that the ward and the form are the same practice. I will hang it back at her station myself. One current remains -- and it runs through someone I do not have the strength to face. You might.

The master is waiting in the Protected Ward. Call him at its challenge marker and defeat him. Don't spend the whole fight trying to hold what he gives you. Leave yourself room to move, and come back when it's finished.

Then take the last lesson with you through the door: do not admire him mid-fight. Everyone does -- it is the opening he waits for. Watch his feet, trade the current between you, and come home. All of you. I will be listening to the conduits until you do.

The best of us. That is not sentiment; it is measurement. He moves the way the form promises -- endless, effortless, both blades one motion. But nothing leaves him anymore. Imagine a river that only accepts. When you see it, you will understand why I sent you to unmake the dams first. He is the last one, and he is beautiful, and he must come down.
The Protected Ward. Use its challenge marker to call the master. He's had a long time to build pressure there. Leave yourself room to move.

Keep moving without letting him set every turn. If you're with companions, relieve whoever needs to breathe. If you're alone, leave yourself a way to break off and recover. Admiring how easily he moves is the pause he's waiting for.
Use the challenge marker in the Protected Ward. Defeat the master, then return to me here. Let yourself rest along the way.

I felt it at dawn. The current turned and came home -- every line in the sublevel at once, like a tide remembering the moon. The ward thinks the kolto pressure fixed itself. We know better. Come here. Tell me it is done; I want to hear it in a voice.
The pressure has eased. I felt it before you came through the door. Take your pay and rest. When you're ready to study Infinite Conduit, we'll begin with what you can afford to let go.
Go back to the beginning. The adepts.
Six adepts, one ledger. The stair opens today.
What is the conduit form?
Where do I find them?
What waits below?
Not yet. Let me sit with this first.
The Infinite Conduit Triage Ward Ledger. The ward can sort its sick again.
The coupler -- walk me through it once more.
Five specialists. The line gets its coupler back.
What does the coupler do?
Where is their practice chamber?
How do the specialists fight?
Not today. The current and I need to talk first.
The Infinite Conduit Kolto Conduit Coupler. It wants its line back.
Say it again, slowly. The warden.
I won't go alone. The warden falls, and the sigil comes home.
Who was he, before?
Where does he hold?
What can he do to us?
Then I'll wait for my companions. He will keep.
The Infinite Conduit Fractured Ward Sigil. The deep ward is draining clean.
The station. Tell me again.
Four teachers of one bad lesson. I'll bring the token home.
Who are the inner circle?
Where is the matron's station?
How do the four defend together?
Let me gather myself first. Their lesson can wait for mine.
The Infinite Conduit Matron's Ward Token. The station is quiet.
Once more. I want every word of it.
I'll face him. We'll end this.
What has he become?
Where will I find the master?
How do we survive him?
Not until my companions stand with me. The river can run a little longer.
It is done. He is defeated, and the river runs through.
